entities.summary: Paulus Aemilius Veronensis, a prominent Italian historian, played a pivotal role in the development of Western historiography during the Renaissance. Born in Verona, Italy, around 1490, Veronensis earned his degree in canon law and went on to become a renowned scholar of classical antiquity. His magnum opus, the 'Commentarii in Historiam B. Augusti,' remains a seminal work in the field of Roman history. Veronensis's writings not only shed light on the Roman Empire but also influenced the rise of humanism and the emergence of modern historiography. His legacy can be seen in the works of later historians, such as Flavio Biondo and Francesco Guicciardini, who built upon his research to create a new generation of historians. Veronensis's contributions to the field of history have had a lasting impact, shaping the way we understand the Roman Empire and its legacy. As a testament to his enduring influence, Veronensis's works continue to be studied and revered by scholars today.
